article_text:

A View From the Easel: Gerardo Rosales

“I often say that my favorite material is the next one, the one I haven’t worked with yet.”

Welcome to the 360th installment of A View From the Easel, a series in which artists reflect on their workspace. This week, Gerardo Rosales paints stories late into the night to the sounds of Chaka Khan and a James Baldwin audiobook.

Want to take part? Check out our submission guidelines and share a bit about your studio with us through this form ! All mediums and workspaces are welcome, including your home studio.

Gerardo Rosales , Houston, Texas

How long have you been working in this space?

Two years.

Describe an average day in your studio.

I don't have a set schedule. I would say that I have two studios: my home, where I sometimes draw and sketch, especially on my computer, and my actual studio. In my studio, I produce larger works or ones that involve more use of paint, where I don't feel like I need to be careful about making a mess. Sometimes I work for long hours, including late at night, or I just go to the studio to look at the work I am doing and think about it. I like to listen to music while I am working. I have a very eclectic taste. At the moment, I am interested in Gregorian chants, Chaka Khan, and Caetano Veloso. I also like to listen to audiobooks and podcasts. I recently finished listening to Before Night Fall s by Reinaldo Arenas, and I am now listening to Giovanni's Room by James Baldwin.

How does the space affect your work?

Space definitely affects the work I produce. From 2000 to 2015, I didn’t have a studio like I have now, so I worked from my living room at home. I produced mainly drawings and small-scale paintings. I also produced works that I could assemble in a gallery and that would become large installations. Around 2016, I was able to have access to bigger spaces, and my work was significantly impacted by this. I started producing large paintings, some as big as 96 by 120 inches. After that, I also started making large-scale wall paintings.

How do you interact with the environment outside your studio?

My studio is in a very large artist studio complex in Houston. I believe there are more than 300 studios here. Having said that, I normally work independently and I don’t feel part of an art community where I am at the moment. I have artist friends in the city whom I meet occasionally to talk about art, our work, and life in general.

What do you love about your studio?

Several things, I like the light and its tall walls. This allows me to expand my ideas into large-scale works, and also to play with the space and create installations throughout the studio. The location is very convenient because I have access to art supply stores and coffee shops. I especially like working in my studio at night because it is quieter and my work flows better.

What do you wish were different?

I wish the studio were more affordable and part of a smaller art community with more like-minded individuals. I also wish I had more opportunities to interact with artists from different areas of expertise, so we could collaborate, exchange knowledge, and learn from one another.

What is your favorite local museum?

I don’t have a favorite local museum. I like several museums in the city for different reasons, and I enjoy what each one has to offer.

What is your favorite art material to work with?

I don’t have a favorite material. I like to experiment and use different materials depending on what is most appropriate for each project. I often say that my favorite material is the next one, the one I haven’t worked with yet.

article_text:
T he scars imprinted on impressionable young minds can never fully fade away. Aiming her lens at a rocky beach thrashed by crashing waves, Maka Gogaladze opens her intimate film with a painful anecdote from her adolescent years. Through on-screen texts against a stormy sky, the Georgian film-maker recalls the time she dumped all of her poems into the garbage. The impulsive decision was a gesture of rebellion against her domineering mother; Gogaladze had wanted her to feel guilty.

This debut feature would appear, at first glance, to be another act of revolt. Putting her mother in front of the camera, Gogaladze asks probing, at times blunt, questions about the strict education thrust on her in childhood. Together, they talk about piano lessons that ended in tears, and tough academic exams that continued to haunt the director well into her adulthood. Their contrasting personalities are fascinatingly revealed across these conversations in all their tension, yet these sequences also represent a moving effort to reach across generational differences.

Gogaladze widens the frame to include a series of observational vignettes shot at various children’s classes in Georgia. The subjects vary – history lessons are sandwiched between ballet and dance sessions – yet the disciplined atmosphere remains the same. Even during art class, teachers leave little room for individual expression or debate. Obedience, rather than dialogue, is the order of the day.

At times, the transition between Gogaladze’s personal story and these external sections feels jarring, requiring extra layers of contextual information. Still, it shows that the film is interested in more than just education. For a nation that has undergone invasion numerous times, it is perhaps understandable that Georgia would place such an emphasis on collectivism. Under pressure to uphold a homogenous national identity, however, childlike wonder and innocence is in danger of being lost permanently.

title_original: As Diplomatic Tensions Persist, British Museum Chairman ‘Optimistic’ on Parthenon Marbles Deal
editorial_title_zh: 尽管外交紧张局势持续，大英博物馆主席对帕台农神庙大理石雕塑达成协议表示“乐观”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 奥斯本于周二表示：“我非常希望我们能达成某种安排，让伦敦收藏的帕台农神庙雕塑能够在雅典展出，但它们必须是共享的。”

article_text:
George Osborne, chairman of the British Museum , has expressed hope that a deal can be struck to share the Parthenon Marbles between Athens and London, despite the two-centuries-long diplomatic feud.

“I’m still optimistic that we can reach an agreement,” Osborne told reporters in Athens on Tuesday. “If everyone enters into it with the spirit of we’re not going to get everything we want, as is always the case with a successful agreement, then there’s a deal to be done.” Related Articles Greek Prime Minister to "Ramp Up" Efforts Related to Parthenon Marbles Return The British Museum Will Extend Its Hours Amid 'Extraordinary' Demand for Bayeux Tapestry

The Parthenon Marbles , made between 447 and 432 BCE by the Greek sculptor Phidias, depict gods and processions in marble relief panels, sculptures, and friezes. They’re also known as the Elgin Marbles, after the Scottish nobleman Lord Elgin, who was the British ambassador to Constantinople. Elgin removed the sculptures from the Acropolis in Athens in 1801, while Greece was under Ottoman occupation. He later sold the sculptures to the British government, which has housed them in the British Museum ever since.

Greece has sought the marbles’ return since gaining independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1832, arguing that Elgin had no legal grounds to remove them. British officials, meanwhile, have cited the British Museum Act 1963, which prohibits the museum from deaccessioning objects in its collection, as justification for retaining the sculptures. Tensions between the two countries have escalated in recent years, fueled by the opening of a dedicated museum for the marbles in Athens and reports of leaks and other preservation concerns in the British Museum’s galleries.

“I very much hope we can come to some arrangement whereby the Parthenon sculptures that are in London can be seen in Athens but they have to be shared,” Osborne said Tuesday. “I know that’s not the position of everyone in Greece, and I understand that and respect that, but that is our position, and so if we want to make progress, it has to be in that spirit.”

Osborne’s comments follow a September op-ed by Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis published in the Guardian , in which he took issue with British Museum director Nicholas Cullinan’s characterization of France’s loan of the Bayeux Tapestry as “a very compelling example of international partnership.” Cullinan had suggested that a similar model of “reciprocal exchange” could be applied to the Parthenon Marbles.

“Nobody would seriously contemplate cutting what survives of the tapestry in two and displaying half in London and half in Bayeux, and claiming this was an adequate way to understand it,” he writes, “Yet that is exactly what happened to the Parthenon sculptures.”

Osborne, a former Chancellor of the Exchequer, has been at the forefront of negotiations between the British Museum and Greece. In 2023, the London institution confirmed that it had been in talks with the Acropolis Museum, saying it was close to finalizing a deal under which the sculptures would return to Greece over time as part of a cultural exchange. The agreement never materialized. Greek Culture Minister Lina Mendoni told reporters days later that Greece would not accept a deal affirming the United Kingdom’s ownership claim. Instead, she proposed an exchange that would ensure treasures from Greek antiquity, including objects of comparable prestige to the Parthenon Marbles, would remain on display in London.

World leaders are set to convene at the EU-UK summit in Brussels next month. Speaking at a conference at the University of Athens on October 6, Mitsotakis suggested that discussions on diplomatic ties between the European Union and the United Kingdom, which voted to leave the bloc in 2016, would involve the British Museum dispute.

“The Parthenon sculptures will be part of this debate. This is not just an issue for Greece, it’s an issue for Europe,” Mitsotakis said.

Iñárritu）的《Digger》中，好莱坞巨星汤姆·克鲁斯展现了罕见的一面：这位演员没有以完美的身姿在动作大片中搏杀，其外表几乎让人认不出来。克鲁斯在片中饰演了一位身家亿万的石油大亨，需要为一场产生深远影响的灾难承担责任。然而，该片的影评迄今为止毁誉参半——汤姆·克鲁斯获得重要奖项的机会也因此降低。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其实，早在《Digger》的首批预告片发布时，一切似乎就已经敲定：汤姆·克鲁斯在片中扮演一个衣着显眼的权力大亨，满嘴脏话、趾高气扬、发出恶魔般的笑声，在名利场中四处穿梭。传统上，各大电影奖项总是格外青睐像克鲁斯这样突破固有戏路的演员——近年来他主要凭借夸张的动作片为人所知，尤其是《碟中谍》（Mission Impossible）系列。", "links": [{"text": "Trailer", "url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qU-7KUMw-tk"}, {"text": "Digger", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/625939/digger-2026"}, {"text": "Tom Cruise", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/person/details/23773/tom-cruise"}, {"text": "Mission Impossible “", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/623834/mission-impossible-the-final-reckoning"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，这位好莱坞演员还花了好几个小时进行特效化妆，并不得不穿上胖子道具服（Fat Suit）以彻底改变外貌。此类形象转变取得成果的例子并不罕见，例如加里·奥德曼（Gary Oldman）在《至暗时刻》（Die dunkelste Stunde）中的表演，他凭借对首相温斯顿·丘吉尔的诠释在2018年赢得了自己的第一座“奥斯卡奖”（Academy Award）。", "links": [{"text": "Die dunkelste Stunde", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/550631/die-dunkelste-stunde"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/bild/filmdb/377237/digger-szenenbild-09.jpeg?t=1789571442", "alt": "《Digger》片场画面", "caption": "几乎让人认不出来的迪格·洛克威尔（Digger Rockwell），由汤姆·克鲁斯（左）饰演（© Warner Bros. Pictures）", "credit": "Filmdienst", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "参差不齐的评价", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，导演亚历杭德罗·冈萨雷斯·伊纳里图（Alejandro González Iñárritu）的新片《Digger》迎来的首批媒体评价却十分参差不齐。如今，德国的电影记者们也得以发表意见——他们的结论同样多少有些令人大失所望。《Filmdienst》的影评也对克鲁斯的表演以及整个演员阵容给予了赞赏，但总的来说，这部以环保为主题的喜剧闹剧仍然显得过于表面化。", "links": [{"text": "Alejandro González Iñárritu", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/person/details/169296/alejandro-gonzalez-inarritu"}, {"text": "Filmdienst-Kritik", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/625939/digger-2026#filmkritik"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "汤姆·克鲁斯在片中饰演迪格·洛克威尔（Digger Rockwell），一位身家亿万的石油大亨兼利己主义者，其无情的贪婪引发了一场灾难：他在格陵兰岛的钻井平台发生爆炸，自此一个巨大的冰山正向北欧移动，并将造成大量人员伤亡。在科学顾问的建议下，他邀请了美国总统及其随行人员参加一场会议，但这场灾难似乎已难以避免。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/bild/filmdb/375321/digger-szenenbild-3.jpg?t=1787757294", "alt": "《Digger》片场画面", "caption": "《Digger》面对大众（© Warner Bros. Pictures）", "credit": "Filmdienst", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "目前，《Digger》所受到的反响呈现出如此两极分化的态势，以至于华纳兄弟影片公司（Warner Bros. Pictures）显然干脆将这些充满争议的反应化为了自身营销的一部分。在一个新的宣传预告片中，该片方有意将截然相反的评价并置：赞美之词如“杰作”（Masterpiece）、“辉煌”（Brilliant）或“宏大”（Magnificent）之后，紧接着便是明显更为负面的评价，如“令人不悦”（Unpleasant）、“令人迷惑”（Baffling）或“令人难忍”（Insufferable）。", "links": [{"text": "Promo-Trailer", "url": "https://x.com/warnerbros/status/2104949461940330943"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "汤姆·克鲁斯还有“奥斯卡”的希望吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影评人的分裂程度究竟有多深，从烂番茄（Rotten Tomatoes）网站的数据也可见一斑。在那里，《Digger》在116篇影评中目前获得了53%的好评率，刚刚过半数。而在Letterboxd上，该片仍然保持着非常稳健的平均分——5星中得3.6星。", "links": [{"text": "Rotten Tomatoes", "url": "https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/digger_2026"}, {"text": "Letterboxd", "url": "https://letterboxd.com/film/digger-2026/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "由于该片反响褒贬不一，“奥斯卡”专家们目前认为汤姆·克鲁斯获得相应电影奖项的机会，已远低于此前许多人的预测。在专门探讨潜在“奥斯卡”竞争者的电影评论家和行业观察家网站Next Best Picture上，克鲁斯目前的排名落在了约翰·马尔科维奇（《Wild Horse Nine》）、安德鲁·斯科特（《Elsinore》）和马特·达蒙（《Die Odyssee》）等演员之后。", "links": [{"text": "Next Best Picture", "url": "https://predictions.nextbestpicture.com/oscars/best-actor"}, {"text": "Wild Horse Nine", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/626889/wild-horse-nine"}, {"text": "Elsinore", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/627141/elsinore"}, {"text": "Die Odyssee", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/625936/die-odyssee-2026"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/bild/filmdb/375319/digger-plakat.jpg?t=1787757293", "alt": "《Digger》海报", "caption": "《Digger》官方海报（© Warner Bros. Pictures）", "credit": "Filmdienst", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，无论是网络电影门户网站的评估，还是所谓电影奖项专家的预测，都并非毫无不确定性。归根结底，这些都只是暂时的快照，在颁奖季的进程中仍可能发生多次变化。然而可以确定的是，《Digger》目前在影评界引发了分歧。这部在多个层面完成转型的讽刺作品究竟能否赢得观众的喜爱，将于1.月1.日见分晓；届时，这部由汤姆·克鲁斯、桑德拉·惠勒（Sandra Hüller）和约翰·古德曼（John Goodman)主演的电影将在德国影院上映。", "links": [{"text": "Digger", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/625939/digger-2026"}, {"text": "Tom Cruise", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/person/details/23773/tom-cruise"}, {"text": "Sandra Hüller", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/person/details/206427/sandra-huller"}, {"text": "John Goodman", "url": "https://www.filmdienst.de/person/details/23525/john-goodman"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
In „Digger“ von Regisseur Alejandro G. Iñárritu präsentiert sich Hollywood-Superstar Tom Cruise von einer ungewohnten Seite: Statt sich in makelloser Form durch ein Action-Spektakel zu kämpfen, ist der Schauspieler äußerlich kaum wiederzuerkennen. Cruise verkörpert darin einen milliardenschweren Erdölmagnaten, der eine folgenschwere Katastrophe zu verantworten hat. Doch die Kritiken zum Film fallen bislang durchwachsen aus – und damit sinken auch Cruises Chancen auf wichtige Auszeichnungen.

Eigentlich war schon alles ausgemacht, als die ersten Trailer von „ Digger “ veröffentlicht wurden: Tom Cruise flucht, stolziert und lacht diabolisch als auffällig gekleideter Machtmogul durch die Manege. Preisverleihungen prämieren es traditionell zu gerne, wenn Schauspieler wie Cruise, aufgefallen in den letzten Jahren vor allem mit seinen extravaganten Actionfilmen, allen voran der „ Mission Impossible “ -Reihe, mit Rollen aus Gewohnheiten ausbrechen.

Dazu kommt noch, dass der Hollywood-Schauspieler stundenlang in der Maske saß und in einen Fat Suit schlüpfen musste, um sich physisch vollständig zu verändern. Dass solche Verwandlungen Früchte tragen, hat man beispielsweise bei Gary Oldman in „ Die dunkelste Stunde “ gesehen, der für seine Darstellung von Premierminister Winston Churchill 2018 seinen ersten „Academy Award“ einfahren konnte.

Durchwachsene Krtiken

Doch die ersten Pressestimmen zu „Digger“ von Regisseur Alejandro González Iñárritu fielen sehr durchwachsen aus. Mittlerweile dürfen sich auch deutsche Filmjournalist:innen äußern – ihre Fazits sind ebenfalls eher ernüchternd. Auch die Filmdienst-Kritik lobt zwar Cruises Darbietung sowie das ganze Ensemble, doch generell bleibt die komödiantische Farce zum Thema Umweltschutz zu oberflächlich.

Tom Cruise spielt darin Digger Rockwell, milliardenschwerer Erdölmagnat und Egomane, dessen rücksichtslose Profitgier für eine Katastrophe sorgt: Seine Bohrplattform in Grönland ist explodiert und fortan bewegt sich ein gigantischer Eisberg auf Nordeuropa zu, der zahlreiche Todesopfer verursachen würde. Auf Anraten seines wissenschaftlichen Beraters lädt er den US-Präsidenten und dessen Gefolgschaft zu einer Konferenz ein, doch das Unglück scheint kaum noch abzuwenden.

Mittlerweile fällt die Rezeption von „ Digger “ derart durchwachsen aus, dass Warner Bros. Pictures die kontroversen Reaktionen offenbar kurzerhand zum Teil der eigenen Vermarktung macht. In einem neuen Promo-Trailer stellt das Studio bewusst gegensätzliche Stimmen nebeneinander: Auf Lob wie „Masterpiece“, „Brilliant“ oder „Magnificent“ folgen unmittelbar deutlich negativere Einschätzungen wie „Unpleasant“, „Baffling“ oder „Insufferable“.

Tom Cruise noch mit „Oscar“-Chancen?

Wie gespalten die Kritiker tatsächlich sind, zeigt auch ein Blick auf Rotten Tomatoes . Dort kommt „Digger“ derzeit auf einen Wert von 53 Prozent bei 116 Kritiken und liegt damit nur knapp über der Hälfte positiver Besprechungen. Wohingegen der Film auf Letterboxd noch eine Durchschnittswertung von sehr soliden 3.6 von 5 Sternen aufweist.

Durch die durchwachsene Rezeption des Films räumen „Oscar“-Experten auch Tom Cruise inzwischen deutlich geringere Chancen auf einen entsprechenden Filmpreis ein, als vielfach zuvor prognostiziert worden war. Auf der Website Next Best Picture , auf der sich Filmkritiker und Branchenbeobachter mit den möglichen „Oscar“-Anwärtern auseinandersetzen, wird Cruise derzeit unter anderem hinter Schauspielern wie John Malkovich („ Wild Horse Nine “), Andrew Scott („ Elsinore “) und Matt Damon („ Die Odyssee “) geführt.

Allerdings sind weder die Einschätzungen von Online-Filmportalen noch die Prognosen vermeintlicher Filmpreis-Experten frei von Unsicherheiten. Letztlich handelt es sich dabei um Momentaufnahmen, die sich im Verlauf der Awards-Saison noch mehrfach verändern können. Fest steht jedoch, dass „ Digger “ die Filmkritik derzeit spaltet. Wie die auf mehreren Ebenen wandelnde Satire beim Publikum ankommt, lässt sich ab dem 1. Oktober herausfinden; dann startet der Film mit Tom Cruise , Sandra Hüller und John Goodman in den deutschen Kinos.

title_original: 【関西プレビュー】「不滅の力 永井豪 –永井豪記念館リバイバル–」京都文化博物館で11月28日から 令和6年能登半島地震復興祈念
editorial_title_zh: 【关西预览】“不灭之力 永井豪 –永井豪纪念馆复活–”11月28日起在京都文化博物馆举办 令和6年能登半岛地震灾后重建祈福展
editorial_excerpt_zh: 京都文化博物馆（京都市）将于11月28日起举办令和6年能登半岛地震灾后重建祈福“不灭之力 永井豪 –永井豪纪念馆复活–”展。展期至2027年1月11日。“魔神Z”、“恶魔人”、“甜心战士”

article_text:
京都文化博物館（京都市）で、令和6年能登半島地震復興祈念「不滅の力 永井豪 –永井豪記念館リバイバル–」が11月28日から開催されます。会期は2027年1月11日まで。

「マジンガーＺ」「デビルマン」「キューティーハニー」……数々の名作で知られるマンガ家・永井豪。その故郷、石川県・輪島市は、2024年1月1日の能登半島地震によって壊滅的な被害を受けました。

本展では、2024年の地震発生当時、永井豪記念館に実際に展示されていた原画・原稿やフィギュア類をはじめ、開館時に展示されていた代表作の原稿、さらに永井豪による本展のための描き下ろしマンガ作品などを展示。輪島市の全面協力のもと、あわせて能登半島、輪島市の復興、その未来を見据えます。

令和6年能登半島地震復興祈念 不滅の力 永井豪 –永井豪記念館リバイバル ETERNAL SPIRITS-GO NAGAI GO! WONDERLAND REVIVAL

会場：京都文化博物館 3階展示室（京都市中京区三条高倉）

会期：2026年11月28日（土）～2027年1月11日（月・祝）

開館時間：10:00～18:00（金曜日は19:30まで） ※入場はそれぞれ閉室の30分前まで

休館日：月曜日（ただし1月11日は開館）、年末年始（2026年12月28日～2027年1月4日）

観覧料：一般1,600円、⼤高⽣1,200円、中小生700円円 ※その他、ペアチケットやグッズ付チケットあり。詳しくは公式サイトをご覧ください

詳しくは 公式サイト へ

注目したい本展の見どころ

本展の大きな見どころは、能登半島地震で被災した「永井豪記念館」から発見された原画・原稿やフィギュア類の展示です。石川県輪島市の観光名所・朝市通りにあった同館は、地震による火災で大きな被害を受け、展示物の焼失も危ぶまれました。しかし、開館当初に施された耐火対策などが功を奏し、外壁が黒く焼け焦げた建物の中から、地震発生当時に展示されていた原画108点とフィギュア類が発見されました。本展では、これらの貴重な作品を公開します。

さらに、2009年の記念館開館時に展示されていた、永井豪のデビュー作を含む名作の原稿も多数展示。加えて、永井豪が本展のために描き下ろした、輪島での思い出を綴ったマンガ原稿を初公開します。令和6年能登半島地震の復興祈念した、まさに不滅の精神を感じさせる内容と言えるでしょう。

「輪島市・能登半島」と「永井豪」

永井豪は、1945年に石川県輪島市で生まれました。幼少期を同地で過ごし、上京後も、輪島市のキャラクター「もんぜんくん」のデザインや、「のと鉄道」や市内のコミュニティバスに永井豪キャラクターがラッピングされるなどのかかわりはもちろんのこと、結婚式の引き出物に輪島漆器を選ぶなど、公私ともに故郷と深いかかわりを持っています。2009年4月25日に同市の朝市通りに「永井豪記念館」が開館して以降は、定期的な訪問を通じて輪島市との交流を重ねました。

同館は、「マジンガーZ」の大型フィギュアや作品の原画など、貴重な資料が多数展示され、毎年約1万2000人が訪れる観光名所となっていました。開館15周年を目前に、2024年1月1日に発生した能登半島地震に被災。その後朝市通りで発生した火災により建物は全焼しましたが、開館時の耐火施策が功を奏し、原画とフィギュア類が発見されました。 （美術展ナビ）

主な展示作品

永井豪 プロフィール

1945年9月6日石川県輪島市生まれ。小学1年生の夏休みに家族と共に東京へ引っ越す。幼少の頃よりマンガ・映画・落語・冒険小説に親しみ、石ノ森章太郎氏のアシスタントを経て、1967年『目明しポリ吉』(ぼくら/講談社)でデビュー。翌年『ハレンチ学園』(少年ジャンプ/集英社)が連載開始となり、たちまち大ブームになる。以後、現在に至る迄、幅広いジャンルの作品を発表し続けている。現在は、『週刊ポスト』誌上にて「柳生裸真剣」、『ビッグコミック』誌上にて「永井豪の幻想怪画」を連載中。最新作として「地球大戦2053」を『漫画ゴラク』にて発表。代表作には『ハレンチ学園』『デビルマン』『マジンガーZ』『キューティーハニー』等多数。

2009年、石川県輪島市に輪島市立永井豪記念館がオープン 2014年、東京アニメアワードフェスティバル アニメ功労賞〈原作者〉 受賞 2016年、第25回日本映画批評家大賞 アニメーション部門 ダイヤモンド大賞 受賞 2018年、第47回日本漫画家協会賞 文部科学大臣賞受賞 2019年、フランス政府より芸術文化勲章(シュヴァリエ)受章 2025年、旭日小綬章受章 2026年、米国で最も権威ある漫画賞の一つ「アイズナー賞」殿堂入り

Perry）执导。 在巨大的太阳耀斑导致文明崩塌的世界里。欧洲失去了国家的框架，各地独裁者为争夺霸权而混战。在此背景下，被称为“总能找到失落之物的男人”的寻宝人杰克，收到了来自英格兰统治者奥古斯特的危险委托。内容是潜入暴君沃尔科夫统治下的法国，寻找列奥纳多·达·芬奇的名画《蒙娜丽莎》。踏入全是不法之徒的死亡禁区的杰克，开始逼近隐藏在《蒙娜丽莎》中的惊人秘密。 《银河护卫队》系列的戴夫·巴蒂斯塔饰演主角杰克，《007：大破量子危机》的欧嘉·柯瑞兰寇、电视剧集《权力的游戏》的克里斯托夫·海维尤以及《复仇者联盟》系列的塞缪尔·L·杰克逊共同出演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2025年制作／105分钟／PG12／美国 原题或英文片名：Afterburn 发行：Starday-Albatross Film 剧场公映日：2026年11月13日", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "演职人员", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "查看全部演职人员", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "故事有些平庸，影像、导演以及结构也有杂乱之处，总觉得差了点意思。 片尾字幕中间虽然有那么点“彩蛋”，但果然还是差了点意思。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "剧透！点击阅读正文", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一个没有价值观的世界。一个连生命都没有价值的的反乌托邦。 但是，正因为是这样的世界，唯独那赤裸裸的“情趣”才是人们生存不可或缺的。哪怕那只是银幕上闪过的平庸物品的质感——。 《Afterburn》开场不久，饰演主角杰克的戴夫·巴蒂斯塔小跑着爬上豪宅楼梯的场景。看到那个身影的瞬间，我总觉得有一种说不出的违和感。 也不知是裤子太紧，还是外套太窄，他看起来比以前我看过的他要苗条得多。也难怪，据说为了健康和戏路，他特意从315磅减到了240磅，这种变化比反乌托邦的背景更加鲜明地跃入眼帘。这导致我的第一印象显得很不自然，让人把世界观抛到脑后，满脑子都在琢磨“他穿的这件机车夹克到底是牛皮、PU还是羊皮”。让人在意得不得了，完全无法忽视。这大概就是中了电影的圈套吧。 顺应这种无聊电影的套路，开始了一场老套的开金库戏码。正当我好奇他是怎么搞到那个情报时，塞缪尔·L·杰克逊饰演的金格（King）这样喃喃道： King: Humor me. ホーム > 作品情報 > 映画「アフターバーン 世紀末の秘宝」

アフターバーン 世紀末の秘宝

劇場公開日： 2026年11月13日

解説・あらすじ

文明崩壊後のヨーロッパを舞台に、人類最後の秘宝をめぐる争奪戦の行方を描いたアクションアドベンチャー。スコット・チッドウッドとポール・エンズによるカルト的人気のグラフィックノベルを原作に、「デイ・シフト」のJ・J・ペリー監督がメガホンをとった。 巨大な太陽フレアによって文明が崩壊した世界。ヨーロッパでは国家の枠組みが失われ、各地で独裁者たちが覇権を争っていた。そんな中、“失われたものを必ず見つける男”と称されるトレジャーハンターのジェイクのもとに、イングランドの支配者オーガストから危険な依頼が舞い込む。その内容は、暴君ヴォルコフが支配するフランスに潜入し、レオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチの名画「モナ・リザ」を探し出すこと。無法者だらけの死の領域に足を踏み入れたジェイクは、モナ・リザに隠された驚くべき秘密に迫っていく。 「ガーディアンズ・オブ・ギャラクシー」シリーズのデイブ・バウティスタがジェイク役で主演を務め、「007 慰めの報酬」のオルガ・キュリレンコ、テレビシリーズ「ゲーム・オブ・スローンズ」のクリストファー・ヒビュ、「アベンジャーズ」シリーズのサミュエル・L・ジャクソンが共演。

2025年製作／105分／PG12／アメリカ 原題または英題：Afterburn 配給：スターキャットアルバトロス・フィルム 劇場公開日：2026年11月13日

How you do it? Jake：Do what? King：I employ dozens to do what you do. But yet you seem to be the only one who finds things others can't. てっか!? それほど都合のいい嗅覚があるのなら、まずは自分の衣装のサイズ感を見つけてほしかったところ。 全体を包むロードムービーっぽい演出も、かえって煩わしく思える。そして極めつけは、秘宝と呼ばれるものを見た瞬間。 ――「なんじゃー！？ こりゃー！？」 ってか!? スリムになって頑張っている彼には悪いけれど、どうにも締まりが悪い。 おまけに前評判では、あのケイジさんも参加するかもね、なんて噂もあった。だから ――「なんじゃー！？ こりゃー！？」 ってか!? （すんません……このディストピア世界、言葉も不足しているので使い回しで） 命の価値はなくても、ツッコミどころの価値だけは残されている。そんな一作です。

article_text:
Taiwanese director Tsao Jui-yuan unveiled his new drama series “ A Time ,” rooted in Taiwan’s campus folk music movement of the 1970s, at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF).

Tsao, known for “Crystal Boys,” “A Touch of Green” and “Seqalu: Formosa 1867,” spent eight years developing the project, which traces four decades of friendship, love and personal transformation.

Related Stories

Lucy Liu’s 'The Pirate Queen' Expands With Graphic Novel, New Game and International Tour as Creator Eloise Singer Joins BAFTA Breakthrough Cohort (EXCLUSIVE)

BAFTA Names Hilary Rosen as Chair

Two generations of actors play five friends at different stages of their lives. Ning Chang, who is an executive producer for the first time, stars alongside “Meteor Garden” star Jerry Yan, Chen Yi-han, Golden Horse best actor winner Wu Kang-ren and Liang Cheng-chun. The younger ensemble features former NCT and WayV member Lucas Wong , Suri Lin, Fandy Fan, Iain Lu and Joseph Huang.

“The starting point for this project was my desire to come to terms with my own youth,” Tsao said. “I’ve always believed that campus folk music is one of the most important cultural IPs in contemporary Taiwan. Against that backdrop, I wanted to tell a story about youth, from youthful recklessness to the different stages of life.”

Written by Chi Hsi-lin, “A Time” follows the five friends after Si Mao is injured diving into an empty swimming pool. As he lies in a coma for decades, the others deal with love, guilt and personal struggles, eventually reuniting as long-buried secrets from their youth come to light.

Tsao likened casting the younger versions of the characters to searching for a needle in a haystack and praised the five newcomers for their performances and commitment.

Chang, who was first approached to act in the series before also taking on the role of executive producer, described Tsao as an “actor scanner,” able to detect even the slightest change in a performer’s emotional state.

Tsao said he invited Chang because of her resilience and commanding presence, qualities that reminded him of Kwak Sin-ae, the Oscar-winning producer of “Parasite.” “She’s actually someone I look up to very much,” Chang said.

Iain Lu, who plays the younger version of Chang’s character, said the director really emphasizes that actors must fully inhabit their characters. “If we lose focus or get distracted, even for a moment, he notices,” Lu said.

Wong, the first Hong Kong-born artist to debut with South Korea’s SM Entertainment, makes his acting debut as the younger Si Mao.

“Being able to work with such an outstanding cast on my first acting project taught me so much,” Wong said. “I also learned diving, guitar and dancing for the role. This performance has been a very meaningful experience for me.”

Joseph Huang, who comes from a musical family and plays the younger Mian Yang, said the dance movements were challenging for all of them, “but we also really enjoyed being able to express ourselves through singing and dancing in addition to acting.”

The five younger cast members performed the Taiwanese folk song “Seasonal Rain” at the press conference, recreating a dance sequence from the drama.

The production brings together more than 30 creative professionals whose work has been recognized by the Golden Horse, Golden Bell and Golden Melody awards, as well as international festivals.

“A Time” is scheduled to premiere in 2027.

hand）的观点。对于你关于体育和欺骗的设想，我的回应方式是——尤其在与历年来的职业运动员交流之后——我一直对围绕职业生涯甚至仅仅是个人福祉的各种计算着迷。这让我相信，艺术家和运动员之间存在相通之处，因为他们都在某种硬核系统中依凭自己的激情或热情生活。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "text": "随着NIL（“姓名、形象、肖像”）制度的引入，这种对话我经常听到，年轻运动员在形象权方面拥有了更多的利害关系和自主空间。我可以想象，随着这些新的谈判自由的到来，事情并未变得单方面地轻松，反而呈现出了升级的监视特性。我想你的《维特鲁威人》正是在这里与此产生关联，因为如今的运动员必须应对超越其自身视角能力的感知可能性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这确实是以最亲密形式存在的身体性，与以最高度中介化（hypermediated）形式存在的媒介化的完美结合。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "再往前看，从某种意义上说，这就是我们在今年早些时候贾斯汀·比伯在科切拉（Coachella）音乐节的表演中所感悟到的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "很有意思。怎么说？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们以一种前所未见的方式，现场见证了那种高度中介化的发生。它极其清晰、极其极简地结晶了出来。所有的舞台布景都被剥离了，以至于被简化到最基础的构成。那仅仅是他身体的独特性，以及他正在重审自己童年所经历的所有中介作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "甚至连他那场表演以及随后的世界杯表演，我都将其视为一种拒绝，它在一个曾作为童工的人的语境下，展现出了某种极其宏大深广的内涵。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对。我在科切拉音乐节上最喜欢的部分是，他唱着自己所有最喜欢的歌，但每一首都不唱完。他会唱到一半就切断。于是他会让全场观众跟着唱，然后又停下来。这几乎就像是一种边缘控制（edging）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "顺着你的观点，他的一生都在被直播，因此他完美地体现了这样一个人：他可以去翻看自己的YouTube视频，并将其呈现给观众。在某种程度上，他现在摆脱了所有其他的滤镜。这样做有着某种与纯真截然相反的特质——一种对坚持纯真的拒绝。我认为这对于作为资本主义系统中的公民说明了许多问题：如果我们能够放弃这种所谓自我纯真的拐杖，我们或许就能以一种不同的方式看待世界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "马克·彼得森（Mark Pieterson）是一位加纳裔美国观念艺术家、独立策展人兼作家，常驻休斯顿和洛杉矶。他是安迪·沃霍尔基金会艺术作家资助金（Andy Warhol Foundation Arts Writers Grant）的获得者。", "translated": true}]

The Choreopolitics of Looking: Interview with Paul Pfeiffer

PAUL PFEIFFER . Photo by Joey Trisolini. Courtesy Perrotin, Los Angeles.

The linguistic associations that emerge from Paul Pfeiffer’s solo exhibition “Olympia,” on view at Perrotin Los Angeles through November 7, are inseparable from the city’s preparations to host the 2028 Olympic Games and the political and cultural significations such an event produces. Yet “Olympia” invokes something older and more metaphysical: Olympus, the mythological seat of the gods, and the summit as a site of transcendence, power, and spectacle. The Olympic “peak” becomes, in Pfeiffer’s work, entangled with the heights manufactured by media, capital, and collective desire. “Soft power is a polite way to describe something that is way more disturbing,” he tells me shortly after the exhibition’s opening.

It is tempting, then, to understand Pfeiffer’s work not simply as an interrogation of visual hierarchy and its ideological production of innocence, but as an attempt to excavate the occult structures beneath its surfaces: the interconnected systems through which image regimes and bodies acquire their seemingly natural authority. He traces part of this inquiry through the Italian neo-Marxist thinker Paolo Virno, whom he cites for his observation that artists access forms of knowledge that are ultimately made legible through institutions. Pfeiffer extends this framework to the athlete. Like the artist, the athlete has specialized capacities, occupying a peculiar position as an exceptional body whose singularity is converted into economic and cultural value.

Pfeiffer’s return to LA, following his 2023 retrospective at the Museum of Contemporary Art (MOCA), thus becomes a proposition for what he describes as a “bigger project,” further examining the narratives and economies of sport, machineries of representation, and their beguiling excess. In “Olympia,” the ascent toward the acme becomes a metaphor for cultural climax itself: a moment that is never simply reached, but staged, circulated, and consumed.

Installation view of PAUL PFEIFFER ’s “Olympia” at Perrotin, Los Angeles, 2026. Photo by Paul Salveson. Courtesy the artist and Perrotin.

“Olympia” is staged like a focused iteration of your 2023 exhibition “Prologue to the Story of the Birth of Freedom” at MOCA . What arrivals and departures motivated this presentation?

The current exhibition at Perrotin really grew out of the MOCA show in a way that was unexpected to me. To some degree, the MOCA show revealed a depth of resonance that I knew was always there in my work, but to have it happen at one of the major institutions really brought it to relief. I mean, that show was 25 years of work. “Olympia” is my first chance to respond more consciously to the LA environment following “Prologue.”

The title, “Olympia,” is borrowed from the title of the 1938 film by Leni Riefenstahl covering the 1936 Olympics in Germany. (Riefenstahl notably claimed a non-political or apolitical status.) So, while this show may be a reduced version of the MOCA exhibition, it comes loaded with the legacy of visual production in its slippery relationship to politics.

I’m sure having the privilege of seeing the works here in that way allowed you to make connections that perhaps previously escaped intuition.

I’m coming to this contemporary scene—the moment, if you will—that we’re all coming to in a very intuitive way. And to me, it’s an occupation with sports and how sports intersect with what’s happened over the 25 past years, which is first the emergence of digital media and then the emergence of social media.

These are ideas that have, for the most part, informed your practice even before the emergence of social media as we know it. What makes this moment of particular interest?

Absolutely. It has been a major subtext of the work, intuitively speaking, since the beginning. We’ve gone through a major wormhole. And in some ways, to me, sports and entertainment have been a very powerful filter to understand where we’re at and what we’ve been through in the last couple of decades.

Details of PAUL PFEIFFER ’s Vitruvian Figure (Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum: Ground Plan) , 2026, black and red graphite on vellum, 169.5 x 205.74 x 7.6 cm, framed. Photos by Paul Salveson. Courtesy the artist and Perrotin, Los Angeles.

This show primarily centers on two works: the sculptural Vitruvian Figure (Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum) (2026) and its accompanying renderings, and a new installment of the Incarnator series (2018– ), which feature fragmented effigies of the popstar Justin Bieber fashioned in historical iconography of Christ. And while the frame of reference for understanding “Olympia” is the Debordian idea of spectacle, the condition that makes this conceit possible is the (re)production of capital. What interests me is how Bieber’s Christ-like representation can offer a simultaneous understanding of capital and images.

It’s funny. You’re making me think in terms of capitalism and democracy as a mythology or religion.

Much like the sacrifice of Christ comes to define the rubrics and metrics of God’s love and grace, Bieber’s challenges as a popstar, essentially a child worker, come to define the success of capitalism. In the same way that Carl Jung in his 1952 book Answer to Job discussed how each trial and tribulation that figures like Abraham, Job, and Jesus endure is a way for God to understand himself, each challenge faced by popstars like Bieber…

Michael Jackson.

Right. These are all ways for capitalism to understand itself. And the images that, in the Debordian sense, mediate social relations are all part of this process.

In fact, if you didn’t have the ups and downs in the process of individuation, it wouldn’t be capitalism, but something completely else. It would be communism. So, it’s interesting that we need the triumph of the individual over hardship for the story to be successful as a mythology that can sustain itself.

Detail of PAUL PFEIFFER ’s Justin Bieber Ecce Homo I (Seville) , 2026, cedar wood, paint, and metal armature, 38.1 x 55.8 x 20.3 cm. Photo by Paul Salveson. Courtesy the artist and Perrotin, Los Angeles.

In thinking through your work, I’ve been developing a theory about sports that moves beyond concerns of fandom and theatrics. Specifically, I find that what generates interest in any sport (even as far back as gladiators) is a performance of deception, structured and psychologically attenuated by an implicit social contract. This deception is non-nefarious and cannot be conflated with the trickster archetype, in that there isn’t an unethical withholding that takes place in the performance. There’s something here that seems to relate more directly with how we interact with social media content, and media in general.

I really love what you’re saying about the athlete and sleight of hand. One way that I would respond to your setup thinking about sports and deception is that I’ve been fascinated—especially after talking to professional athletes over the years—about the kinds of calculations around career or even just personal well-being. It has led me to believe that artists and athletes are connected in the ways both live out of their passions or their enthusiasm in a kind of hardcore system.

PAUL PFEIFFER , Vitruvian Figure (Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum) , 2026, digital video (color, silent) and custom LED display, 48.26 x 96.5 cm (left); and detail of Vitruvian Figure (Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum: Elevations) , 2026, black and red graphite on vellum, 169.5 x 205.7 x 7.6 cm, framed (right). Photos by Paul Salveson. Courtesy the artist and Perrotin, Los Angeles.

For sure. And, you know, I guess in a way the only separation here is that while artists operate in this nebulous zone, the athlete focuses more on the objective metrics that sustain their organization.

Although I will say, something that I noticed—from the times that I’ve had an opportunity to talk with younger professional athletes—is that they’re more attuned to the game of it all . Since they’re growing up in the age of social media.

True.

And the nature of communication and certain choices that you would have to make, in which your life could go one way or another.

This is a conversation that I keep hearing especially with the introduction of NILs (“name, image, likeness”), where the younger athletes have more stakes in and latitude with image rights. I can imagine things don’t get unilaterally easier with these new negotiation freedoms, but rather present updated surveillance features. I think this is where your Vitruvian Figure is implicated, for the athlete now must contend with perceptive possibilities that exceed the capabilities of their vantage point.

For starters, as digital media was emerging in the early 2000s, there was a thought that I was receptive to—this idea that the athlete is, in an existential sense, really a crystallization of the every-person situation in the advent of digital media. That something was about to happen, in which everything that already existed about our individual relationship being enmeshed in systems was about to be expanded.

Absolutely. But, in a way, athletes maybe have a little bit of privileged information toward that understanding.

To me, the image of the athlete in all of their physicality and performance, within the markings of the court, and under the intense lights of the arena, and with all the cameras watching—that, to me, just becomes the existential condition in a hypervisual form.

PAUL PFEIFFER , Justin Bieber San Juan de la Cruz (Seville), 2026, cedar wood, paint, and metal armature, 49.5 x 26.6 x 15.2 cm (left); and Justin Bieber Legs Crucified (Seville), 2026, cedar wood, paint, and metal armature, 118.1 x 50.8 x 45.7 cm (right). Photos by Paul Salveson. Courtesy the artist and Perrotin, Los Angeles.

It’s really the perfect marriage of physicality in its most intimate form, with mediation in its most hypermediated form.

And just to jump forward, it is, in a way, that thing we all intuit in Justin Bieber’s performance at Coachella earlier this year.

Interesting. How so?

We saw that hypermediation happening live in a way we hadn’t quite seen before. It crystallized so much so clearly, and so minimally. All the staging was removed, so that it was reduced just to the most fundamental formulation. It’s just the specificity of his body, with all the mediation that he’s reviewing from his own childhood.

I even registered that performance and his subsequent World Cup performance as a kind of refusal that revealed something deeply capacious within the context of him being a former child worker.

Yeah. What I loved about this part at Coachella is that he was going through all his favorite songs, but he wouldn’t finish any of them. He would cut it off halfway through. So, he would get the whole crowd singing and then stop it. It was almost like edging.

And to your point, his whole life has been live-streamed, and so he’s the perfect embodiment of someone who can look up their own YouTube videos and present them to the audience. And he’s now free of all other filters, to an extent. There’s something that’s like the opposite of innocence about doing that—a kind of a refusal of the insistence on innocence. I think this says a lot about being a citizen in the capitalist system: if we could only forgo this kind of crutch of supposed self-innocence, we might see the world in a different way.

Mark Pieterson is a Ghanaian American conceptual artist, independent curator, and writer based between Houston and Los Angeles. He is a recipient of the Andy Warhol Foundation Arts Writers Grant.
excerpt_original: On the occasion of Paul Pfeiffer’s solo exhibition at Perrotin LA, Mark Pieterson spoke with the artist about the entangled visual economies of sports, pop culture, and religion. MARK PIETERSON

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Armie Hammer is starring in the under-the-radar action-thriller Tokyo Blitz , which recently wrapped in Los Angeles.

This marks the Call Me By Your Name and The Social Network actor’s first announced project since his controversial Citizen Vigilante film caused a stir this summer after getting the backing of Elon Musk.

Hammer continues to rebuild after years in the wilderness. CAA helped broker the deal for him to join Tokyo Blitz , but agency sources tell us CAA isn’t repping the actor who hasn’t had agency representation since he was dropped by WME in 2021.

Related Stories

Dylan Douglas' Movie Debut 'The Hit On Hitler' Heads To AFM With Bleiberg, First Look

YA Vampire Adaptation 'House Of Night' Gets New Director, Casting Underway & Shoot Eyed For Early 2027

Film Mode Entertainment has boarded worldwide sales on Tokyo Blitz and will be showing a first look to buyers at next month’s American Film Market.

Watch on Deadline

Written and directed by Garrett Glassell ( Kade ), the movie “follows a ruthless Yakuza enforcer (Joey Chase) who’s trying to save his fractured family when he’s drawn into a deadly war for control of Tokyo’s first legal casino, putting him on a collision course with Rick (Armie Hammer), an elite American hitman who never misses his mark.”

The film also stars Kooper Seewald, Yuwi, Nobuaki Shimamoto and John Kim.

Keli Price produced under his Price Productions banner alongside Tommy Anderson of Charthouse Films and Liam S. Terlecki. Executive producers include Clay Epstein of Film Mode Entertainment, Christopher Manalo and Mike Levenson.

“ Tokyo Blitz is an action thriller with real heart at its core, and Garrett has created a distinctive world that feels both visceral and deeply personal. He has a unique style and vision, and pairing that vision with Armie couldn’t have been a better fit,” said Price.

Said Epstein: “Armie brought tremendous intensity and commitment to the role. We’re thrilled to have Film Mode bringing Tokyo Blitz to the international marketplace and giving buyers their first look at AFM .”

Price negotiated Hammer’s deal with CAA and brokered the Film Mode pact. Hammer is repped by law firm Yorn Levine. Chase is repped by NTA; Seewald by Elégance; Yuwi by Park Noack; and Shimamoto by Minc.

"text": "在过去的5十年里，关于约翰·伯格（John Berger）的讨论已经够多了，再添新说几乎让人觉得老生常谈。你知道那些熟悉的共识：这位评论家兼小说家教会了我们如何观看和专注，坚信艺术属于人民，并揭示了男性凝视如何塑造我们的认知。因此，汤姆·奥弗顿（Tom Overton）的一本新传记能够同时捕捉到伯格的影响力范围，并将其重新塑造成一个首先是有血有肉的人，这实在令人惊叹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作家梅根·奥格雷迪（Megan O’Grady）在其近期出版的著作《活着的滋味：与艺术及自我的相遇》（How It Feels to Be Alive: Encounters with Art and Our Selves）中探讨了许多与伯格相同的问题，她为这本传记及其处理这位近乎神话化人物复杂个人生活的方法写了一篇细腻的评论。这是一篇辛酸、耳目一新的阅读体验，也让我想起了围绕詹姆斯·鲍德温（James Baldwin）等艺术家和作家被神圣化的讨论，他们的作品在这个过程中往往被平面化了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实上，我们如何讲述一个艺术家生前（及身后）的故事，很可能是我们这个月最关注的核心。劳伦·莫亚·福特（Lauren Moya Ford）阅读了一位学者对被奉为经典的维米尔（Vermeer）的新颖研究方法，探寻其标志性的叙事模棱两可性在不同媒介和形式中的影响。与此同时，拉维尼亚·梁（Lavinia Liang）则探讨了一本关于多萝西娅·坦宁（Dorothea Tanning）的传记，以及它如何处理她与身为艺术家的丈夫马克斯·恩斯特（Max Ernst）的关系——这也是任何试图将一位被忽视的女艺术家的遗产从其男性伴侣阴影中解放出来的作家所面临的永恒困境。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Books Newsletter", "links": [{"text": "Books Newsletter", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/tag/books-newsletter/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Art Books on Needles and Threads"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "We recommend titles on fiber art, weaving, and textiles, plus Megan O’Grady on a new John Berger biography."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "So much has been said about John Berger over the past five decades that it almost feels trite to pile on. You know the familiar takeaways: that the critic and novelist taught us how to look and pay attention, believed art belongs to the people, exposed how the male gaze shapes our perception. So, it’s especially astounding that a new biography by Tom Overton has managed to both capture the scope of Berger’s influence and reframe him, first and foremost, as human."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Author Megan O’Grady, who reflects on many of the same questions as Berger in her recent book How It Feels to Be Alive: Encounters with Art and Our Selves , penned a sensitive review of the biography and its approach to addressing the complex personal life of this near-mythologized figure. It’s a poignant, refreshing read, and reminds me of the conversation around the sanctification of artists and writers like James Baldwin, whose work gets flattened in the process."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In fact, how we tell the story of an artist’s life (and afterlife) just might be our primary preoccupation this month. Lauren Moya Ford reads one scholar’s novel approach to the canonized Vermeer, searching for the influence of his signature narrative ambiguity across mediums and forms. Meanwhile, Lavinia Liang grapples with a biography of Dorothea Tanning and its treatment of her relationship with her artist husband, Max Ernst, a perennial dilemma facing any author who seeks to move an overlooked woman’s legacy out of the shadow of her male partner."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "More from our critics below, plus a round-up of some of our favorite recent art books on textiles, fabric, and fiber art. One of my personal go-tos is Stories in the Seams: A People’s History of Black Quilts and Their Makers by the wonderful Sharbreon Plummer, and we also recommend books on Palestinian embroidery, Diné weaving, and the Bayeux Tapestry. Read up, and let us know what’s on your list this month!"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "—Lakshmi Rivera Amin, associate editor, books"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/2026/10/textile-books.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "12 Must-Read Books on Textiles and Fiber Art", "links": [{"text": "12 Must-Read Books on Textiles and Fiber Art", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/12-must-read-books-on-textiles-and-fiber-art/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There’s a reason the lexicon of textiles and fiber lends itself so well to storytelling — we thread the needle, weave the tale, spin the yarn. Writers have reached for these metaphors for centuries because they feel true to life, but artists know they’re also true to craft and its tangled histories. We’ve gathered a few recent books on embroidery, fiber art, weaving, and more that deserve a closer look, from Black Southern quilting and Korean bojagi to Palestinian tatreez and contemporary Diné weaving. article_text:
Books Newsletter

Art Books on Needles and Threads

We recommend titles on fiber art, weaving, and textiles, plus Megan O’Grady on a new John Berger biography.

So much has been said about John Berger over the past five decades that it almost feels trite to pile on. You know the familiar takeaways: that the critic and novelist taught us how to look and pay attention, believed art belongs to the people, exposed how the male gaze shapes our perception. So, it’s especially astounding that a new biography by Tom Overton has managed to both capture the scope of Berger’s influence and reframe him, first and foremost, as human.

Author Megan O’Grady, who reflects on many of the same questions as Berger in her recent book How It Feels to Be Alive: Encounters with Art and Our Selves , penned a sensitive review of the biography and its approach to addressing the complex personal life of this near-mythologized figure. It’s a poignant, refreshing read, and reminds me of the conversation around the sanctification of artists and writers like James Baldwin, whose work gets flattened in the process.

In fact, how we tell the story of an artist’s life (and afterlife) just might be our primary preoccupation this month. Lauren Moya Ford reads one scholar’s novel approach to the canonized Vermeer, searching for the influence of his signature narrative ambiguity across mediums and forms. Meanwhile, Lavinia Liang grapples with a biography of Dorothea Tanning and its treatment of her relationship with her artist husband, Max Ernst, a perennial dilemma facing any author who seeks to move an overlooked woman’s legacy out of the shadow of her male partner.

More from our critics below, plus a round-up of some of our favorite recent art books on textiles, fabric, and fiber art. One of my personal go-tos is Stories in the Seams: A People’s History of Black Quilts and Their Makers by the wonderful Sharbreon Plummer, and we also recommend books on Palestinian embroidery, Diné weaving, and the Bayeux Tapestry. Read up, and let us know what’s on your list this month!

—Lakshmi Rivera Amin, associate editor, books

12 Must-Read Books on Textiles and Fiber Art

There’s a reason the lexicon of textiles and fiber lends itself so well to storytelling — we thread the needle, weave the tale, spin the yarn. Writers have reached for these metaphors for centuries because they feel true to life, but artists know they’re also true to craft and its tangled histories. We’ve gathered a few recent books on embroidery, fiber art, weaving, and more that deserve a closer look, from Black Southern quilting and Korean bojagi to Palestinian tatreez and contemporary Diné weaving. Refreshingly, so many of these titles complicate or refuse reductive, familiar frameworks and open up new ways to understand the meditative and political dimensions of textile traditions, moving past the false dichotomy of “craft versus art” and sexist and tired notions of “women’s work.” You might even say these books piece together a new history of textile art, stitch by stitch.

Read More

Discover R. Buckminster Fuller’s Intuition

New from David Zwirner Books: R. Buckminster Fuller’s lyrical case for intuition as the force uniting the sciences and the arts. Originally written in 1968 by the creator of the geodesic dome, this concise work returns with a new introduction by Anahid Nersessian as part of the ekphrasis series.

Learn more

From Our Critics

John Berger in His Own Bruised Time

The late novelist and art critic asked Tom Overton to wait to write his biography until after his death. The result is deeply informative, deferential, and perceptive, sometimes lyrically so. | Megan O’Grady

Read More

Finding Vermeer in Unexpected Places

Artists, filmmakers, poets, and the art market itself still bear traces of the Dutch painter’s influence, writes historian Ruth Bernard Yeazell. | Lauren Moya Ford

Read More

The Trafficker Who Furnished the Museums of LA

A team of researchers excavates the story of Earl Stendahl, a mid-century gallerist who shamelessly stole ancient Mesoamerican objects and marketed them to the institutional art world. | Armando Pulido

Read More

Dorothea Tanning Beyond Max Ernst’s Shadow

A new biography attempts to make the case for Tanning’s independence and artistic strength in her own right, but remains frustratingly tethered to her husband. | Lavinia Liang

Read More

Bold New Books in Art and Visual Culture from the MIT Press

From activist art and trans aesthetics to lowriders, global skateboarding culture, and Vilém Flusser’s prescient vision of the screen age.

Learn more

In the News

Authors Alana Hadid and Jenan Matari pulled their children’s book on Palestine from Penguin after the editors reportedly asked them to temper the language they used to describe decolonial history. Happily, the title is now going to InterLink Books, the only Palestinian-owned publisher in the United States, run by author Hannah Moushabeck and her family.

In related news, bookstores in the United Kingdom are rushing to get copies of Sally Rooney’s novels from distributors after the government banned the sale of her books over her support for Palestine Action.

Required Reading

For Hyperallergic , Isabella Segalovich interviewed journalist, champion of the avant-garde, and Pop-art connoisseur Joan Kron ahead of the release of her memoir, fabulously titled The Renegade Housewives of Pop Art: A Memoir of The 1960s , coming out in December from Pointed Leaf Press.

Alissa Quart reflects on 25 years since the publication of Nickel and Dimed by the late Barbara Ehrenreich, with whom she co-founded the Economic Hardship Reporting Project, for the Nation .

Architecture writer Kate Wagner tackles a new book chronicling the inequality of American public bathrooms for an article in the Baffler with a perfect title.

Rosalyn Drexler is everywhere this fall, particularly in New York. Essayist Leslie Camhi writes in the New Yorker about the late artist and author’s resurgence in galleries, bookstores, and museums across the city.

What We're Reading

Lakshmi Rivera Amin, associate editor, books I’m digging into Story Telling: A Writing Life (2026), Isabel Allende’s new memoir of nearly five decades spent on her craft (thank you to the unusually short hold queue at the Brooklyn Public Library). At 84, she speaks plainly about approaching death; not fearfully or morosely but with reverence for the life she has led and the writing that animates it. I do find it telling that the original Spanish title is La Palabra Mágica: Una Vida Escrita . “The Magic Word” certainly feels more true to Allende’s literary worlds. Maybe I should put a library hold on a Spanish copy, too …

Lisa Yin Zhang, associate editor Halloween’s coming up, so you know I had to revisit a ghost story that one could argue invented the form: Henry James’s The Turn of the Screw (1898).

From the Archive

John Berger Lost His Eyesight to Cataracts and Learned to See

After being afflicted with cataracts, the late critic and novelist reflected on the mechanics of sight. | Melissa Holbrook Pierson

article_text:
目にも鮮やかな花鳥画を中心に、国内外で高い人気を誇る渡辺省亭です。

作品は華やかなイメージですが、若い時期は苦難の連続だったのですね。その後の成功を支えた確かな造形は、青年期の厳しい修練が裏付けにあったのでしょう。

ろくに着物も買えない時期もあったとは…。画壇の付き合いはほどほどに、画業に専念した生涯でした。

title_original: Le mie opere parleranno da sole: così Artemisia diventò una immortale Giuditta
editorial_title_zh: “我的作品会自己说话”：阿尔泰米西亚如何成为不朽的朱迪思
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在期待已久的佛罗伦萨无辜者博物馆展览开幕之际，我们通过阿尔泰米西亚·真蒂莱斯基最具代表性的作品，重温她的生平与艺术。本文原载于…

article_text:
Giuditta tiene la testa di Oloferne con la calma di chi ha già saldato un conto in sospeso. Nessun tremore, nessuna smorfia, solo la determinazione silenziosa di chi non torna indietro. Artemisia Gentileschi dipinse questa scena nel 1612, lo stesso anno del processo per stupro contro Agostino Tassi , durante il quale venne sottoposta a tortura per dimostrare di aver detto la verità sulla violenza subìta a diciassette anni dall’uomo che era pittore come il padre di lei. Dopo aver difeso la propria onestà, Artemisia lasciò Roma e andò a Firenze, dove arrivò nel 1613.

Figlia di Orazio Gentileschi , era cresciuta nella bottega paterna mostrando un talento che superava quello dei fratelli. Lo stupro, il processo pubblico, la tortura, il matrimonio combinato, avrebbero potuto schiacciare chiunque. Non lei. A Firenze , trovò qualcosa che Roma le aveva negato, ovvero la possibilità di essere giudicata per quello che dipingeva, non per quello che le era accaduto.

Giuditta che decapita Oloferne

Una trasformazione, la sua, testimoniata soprattutto da tre opere che, più di altre, ne restituiscono la portata. La prima è Giuditta che decapita Oloferne , dipinta tra il 1612 e il 1613 e oggi agli Uffizi, una delle versioni più intense e fisicamente crude di questo soggetto nella pittura dell’epoca. Nel dipinto, Giuditta e la sua ancella non hanno esitazioni: tengono fermo il generale assiro con una determinazione muscolare che non ha nulla di allegorico.

Chi ha studiato gli atti del processo, ha notato qualcosa che le fonti non confermano, ma che molti storici dell’arte hanno osservato: il volto di Oloferne somiglia a quello di Agostino Tassi, e quello di Giuditta ad Artemisia. Se fosse vero, sarebbe uno dei gesti più radicali nella storia della pittura. Se anche non lo fosse, il quadro resta comunque un’opera di forza rara: la violenza non come soggetto, ma come strumento di verità.

Allegoria dell’Inclinazione

La seconda è l’ Allegoria dell’Inclinazione , realizzata nel 1616 e commissionata da Michelangelo Buonarroti il Giovane (scrittore e letterato, noto per la parentela con il più celebre zio) per la Camera della Fama di Casa Buonarroti . Una figura femminile nuda, una stella in mano, lo sguardo rivolto verso l’alto. È la prima grande commissione pubblica che Artemisia ricevette a Firenze nello stesso anno in cui fu ammessa all’Accademia delle Arti del Disegno, prima donna nella storia dell’istituzione. Un riconoscimento che non aveva precedenti, in una città e in un’epoca in cui le donne artiste erano tollerate, ma non certamente celebrate.

Autoritratto come Santa Caterina d’Alessandria

La terza è l’ Autoritratto come Santa Caterina d’Alessandria , del 1615-17 circa, uno dei dipinti più enigmatici e personali della sua produzione fiorentina. Artemisia si ritrae nei panni della martire cristiana, una donna che aveva resistito al potere imperiale e ne portava i segni sul corpo. Non è un autoritratto celebrativo, ma piuttosto una dichiarazione di identità. La ruota dentata che avrebbe dovuto uccidere Caterina è lì, accanto a lei. Ma lei guarda altrove.

Artemisia, la storia dell’arte e Firenze

A Firenze, Artemisia frequentò la corte medicea, dialogò con intellettuali e scienziati — tra cui Galileo Galilei , con cui ebbe uno scambio epistolare — e costruì una rete di relazioni che nessuna pittrice del suo tempo aveva saputo tessere con la stessa abilità. Fu la scrittrice e storica dell’arte Anna Banti , nel 1947, a restituirle piena dignità letteraria con il romanzo Artemisia , un libro scritto due volte, dopo che il manoscritto originale andò distrutto durante i bombardamenti di Firenze nel 1944. Ma, già nel 1916, il critico d’arte Roberto Longhi , marito della Banti, aveva richiamato l’attenzione su di lei nel saggio Gentileschi padre e figlia . Due voci critiche, quelle dei coniugi Longhi, che insieme avevano cominciato a restituire ad Artemisia il posto che meritava.

La mostra Artemisia Gentileschi a Firenze , aperta al Museo degli Innocenti dal 21 ottobre 2026 al 4 aprile 2027, e curata da Costantino d’Orazio , Cristina Acidini e Sandro Bellesi , si concentra per la prima volta specificamente sul periodo fiorentino, quello della maturità artistica, della libertà conquistata e del riconoscimento pubblico della pittrice. In mostra anche due capolavori di Caravaggio , il maestro di cui Artemisia aveva assorbito la lezione della luce radente e delle figure che emergono dal buio. Un confronto che non schiaccia, ma illumina e dice tanto delle sue origini e di quanto lontano era arrivata.

«Le mie opere parleranno da sole», scrisse al collezionista Don Antonio Ruffo nel 1649. È ancora questa la chiave migliore per varcare la soglia di questa mostra: lasciare che i quadri raccontino la donna e l’artista, senza che la biografia esaurisca tutto il resto.

article_text:
エジプトで約3500年前の岩窟墓を発見。ヒエログリフが明かす高官と家族たちの姿｜エジプト・サッカラのブバステイオン墓地で、新王国時代に造られた3基の岩窟墓が発見された。壁に刻まれたヒエログリフから、約3500年前を生きた高官たちやその家族の経歴、近東との軍事・外交関係が浮かび上がる。【続きを読む】Photo: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities.

発掘調査の様子。Photo: Facebook/Ministry of Tourism and Antiquitiesا

発掘調査の様子。Photo: Facebook/Ministry of Tourism and Antiquitiesا

墓内の壁に施されたレリーフ。Photo: Facebook/Ministry of Tourism and Antiquitiesا

墓内の様子。Photo: Facebook/Ministry of Tourism and Antiquitiesا

100年前の出土品、エジプト最古の回転工具と判明──6000年前の高度な技術と交易も示唆｜約100年前に発掘され、ケンブリッジ大学考古学・人類学博物館に所蔵されている小さな銅合金製の遺物が、エジプト最古の回転式穿孔工具だったことが新たな分析で明らかになった。先王朝時代にさかのぼるこの発見は、当時の職人技術の高度さに加え、長距離交易ネットワークの存在を示す可能性もある。【続きを読む】Photo: Metropolitan Museum of Art

古代エジプトの貴重な考古遺物36点がアメリカから返還。彫像、壁画、写本等の画像を公開｜エジプト観光・考古省は11月6日、同国から不法に持ち出された36点の考古学的遺物を、アメリカの検察当局との協力で回収したと発表。古代エジプトから古代ローマ時代にかけての彫像、壁画、写本など、貴重な遺物の画像が公開された。【続きを読む】 古代エジプト第18王朝時代（紀元前1550年頃〜1292年頃）の石板。Photo: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

メトロポリタン美術館から返還された25点の希少なコプト語・シリア語写本の1つ。Photo: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

古代ローマ時代（西暦1世紀頃〜4世紀頃）の彫像の頭部。Photo: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

エジプトで紀元前300年頃の「魚の塩漬け工場」跡を発見！｜エジブトの西部ナイル・デルタの2遺跡から、紀元前300年頃の工房群とローマ時代の埋葬施設が見つかった。工房群からは約1万点の魚骨も出土しており、考古学者らは、当時の産業活動と生活実態への理解を深める発見と評価している。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

クレオパトラの墓に新たな手がかりか。水没した港と地下トンネルを発見した研究者は「時間の問題」｜エジプト・アレクサンドリア西郊、タップ・オシリス・マグナ神殿遺跡のある海岸部の沖合で、水没した古代の港が見つかった。2022年の地下トンネル発掘に続き、クレオパトラの墓を発見する鍵になるものと考古学者らは見ている。【続きを読む】Photo: DEA / G. DAGLI ORTI/De Agostini via Getty Images

イエスが病を癒す壁画も──宗教の変遷を物語る古代エジプトの遺跡を発見｜エジプトの西方砂漠にあるハルガ・オアシスで、西暦3世紀から7世紀にかけてのものと見られる都市の遺構が見つかった。古代エジプトに初期キリスト教が浸透したコプト時代を知る手がかりとなる建造物や遺物が出土している。【続きを読む】Photo: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

エジプトの古代都市から3人の高級官僚の豪華な墓が出土。碑文が所有者特定の鍵に｜エジプト観光・古代史省が、ルクソールのネクロポリスから新王国時代（第18～20王朝時代、紀元前1539年頃から1077年頃）の3人の高級官僚の墓が発見された。【続きを読む】Photo: Egypt Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities/AP

古代エジプトの「青色」が千年の眠りから目覚める！ アメリカの研究チームが完全再現に成功｜アメリカ・ワシントン州立大学が率いる研究チームが、古代エジプトの幻の合成顔料「エジプシャンブルー」の再現に成功した。【続きを読む】Photo: Bildagentur-online/Schoening/Universal Images Group via Getty Images

古代エジプトの「魂の家」から手形発見。4000年前の職人技を伝える稀少な資料｜約4000年前に作られた古代エジプトの粘土製模型「魂の家」から、人の手形が見つかった。埋葬用に使われたこの模型には、制作時に誤って触れたとみられる職人の痕跡が残されていた。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy of The Fitzwilliam Museum

「魂の家」の底面。左下の部分に手形があるという。Photo: Courtesy of The Fitzwilliam Museum

手形部分のクロースアップ。Photo: Courtesy of The Fitzwilliam Museum

前面には食べ物などが供えられた。Photo: Courtesy of The Fitzwilliam Museum

紀元前に建てられたエジプト軍事施設の建築様式と役割が明らかに｜エジプト北部のシナイ砂漠にある遺跡、テル・アブ・サイフィで数十年前に発見された要塞の全貌を解明する新たな手がかりが見つかった。発掘調査によって、高度な要塞システムや石灰岩の道、兵士の宿舎が姿を現した。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy of Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

要塞へと続く道も発見されており、この下にはプトレマイオス朝に敷かれた道が埋まっている可能性がある。Photo: Courtesy of Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

ラムセス3世の碑文をヨルダン南部の岩壁で発見！｜エジプト王ラムセス3世の碑文がヨルダン南部で発見され、ファラオの影響力がアラビア半島まで及んでいたことが証明された。この発見は古代エジプトの交易ネットワークと地域支配の実態を解明する重要な手がかりとなる。【続きを読む】Photo: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images

ワディ・ラム砂漠で発見されたラムセス3世のカルトゥーシュ。Photo: Jordanian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

世界最古のピラミッドで古代エジプト王子の墓を発見｜エジプトのサッカラで古代エジプト王子の墓が発見され、複数の重要な遺物も出土した。その中には異なる時代のものも含まれており、古代エジプトの埋葬施設が長期間にわたって再利用されていたことを裏付けている。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

ありえない場所から古代エジプト新王国時代の集落跡を発見！｜フランス国立科学研究センターの研究者らは、エジプトのマリウト湖近くのコム・エル・ヌグスで、約3500年前の古代エジプト新王国時代の集落跡を発見した。専門家は「同時代におけるエジプト西部国境の歴史を完全に書き替えるものだ」と語る【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy of Sylvain Dhennin/Antiquity

発見された、ラムセス3世のカルトゥーシュが刻まれた金の指輪。Photo: Instagram/Luxor Times

まるで創世神話の1シーン！ 最新調査で、古代エジプト・カルナック神殿は「島」にあったことが判明｜エジプト・ルクソール近郊にあるカルナック神殿で、この地域における初の包括的な地質考古学調査が行われた。その結果、初期のカルナックは河川の浸食により出現した島状の地形であったことや、中王国時代に始まったと考えられていたこの地域への人々の居住が300年以上も前の古王国時代から行われていたことが明らかになった。【続きを読む】Photo: NurPhoto via Getty Images

ツタンカーメン以来100年ぶりの快挙！ 謎の王トトメス2世の墓を発見｜エジプト観光・遺跡省は、古代エジプトのファラオ、トトメス2世の墓を発見したと発表した。これは1922年にイギリスの考古学者ハワード・カーターによってツタンカーメン王の墓が発見されて以来、実に103年振りの王族の埋葬室の発見となる。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

古代エジプトのミイラは高級スパの香りがした!?｜ユニバーシティ・カレッジ・ロンドン（UCL）とスロベニアのリュブリャナ大学による研究チームがカイロのエジプト博物館に展示・保管されている5000年前の古代エジプトのミイラから放たれる香りを調査した結果、「高級スパ」のような香りであったと発表した。【続きを読む】Photo: Oli Scarff/Getty Images

ギザの大ピラミッドを作業員が打ち砕く動画がSNSで炎上｜ギザの大ピラミッドでハンマーやノミなどの道具を使って作業する作業員の動画がソーシャルメディアで拡散された後、「管理のずさんさ」を非難するエジプト学者やエジプト議会が声明を発表するなど物議を醸している。【続きを読む】Photo: Anadolu via Getty Images

"自2007年以来，石坂一直负责该电影节的亚洲电影节目策划，当时大部分参赛作品仍采用胶片拍摄。几年之内，数字技术便全面普及。他的选片流程从35毫米拷贝和VHS录像带转向了DVD，后来又演变为流媒体链接和可下载的审看样片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "《综艺》热门内容", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“物理介质让位于数据；电影失去了有形的‘分量’，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一转变也改变了电影的外观。摆脱了重新装填胶片的需要，亚洲导演们开始倾向于由一气呵成的长镜头构成的长片时长，所谓的慢电影（slow cinema）也在该地区传播开来。其中的两位领军大师在2010年代的大型欧洲电影节上摘得最高奖项：泰国的阿彼察pong·韦拉斯哈古凭借《能召回前世的布米叔叔》斩获戛纳金棕榈奖，菲律宾的拉夫·迪亚兹则凭借《离开的女人》夺得威尼斯金狮奖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "石坂还负责监督电影节旨在扶持年轻亚洲电影人的“亚洲之窗”竞赛单元。今年入围的10部作品包括菲律宾卡茨基·弗洛雷斯的《Edjop》、韩国金贤民的《高地之上》以及印度切兹扬的《纸花》。哈萨克斯坦阿扎マット·沙尔吉恩的《Shyrmauyq》、印度尼西亚阿里亚尼·达玛万的《Jani Be Good》以及日本鲸冈弘纪的《Saravah》也同样在竞争之列。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他说，大制片厂作品与独立电影之间的界限已经大大模糊。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“例如在菲律宾——一个常被形容为自2005年以来正经历其‘第三黄金时代’的国家电影产业——我们看到主流明星在爱上大胆、原创的剧本后，积极加入独立电影项目，”石坂说，“这甚至催生了一个混成词‘主流独立电影’（maindie）。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他指出，布里兰特·门多萨和容·罗布斯·拉纳等导演在商业片和小成本独立片之间游刃有余，是连接这两个世界的关键纽带。该地区的其他电影产业也正经历着类似的跨界融合。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果说2010年代属于东南亚电影，那么2020年代的故事仍在书写之中。目前，石坂特别提到了台湾和韩国，称赞它们在公共资金和体制支持方面实力雄厚。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“在主题方面，来自中国自治区——西藏、内蒙古和新疆——的一股令人兴奋的新锐电影人浪潮正步入聚光灯下，”他说，“在已故先驱万玛才旦等开拓者的指导和启发下，这些导演带来了鲜明的地域视角和美学审视，使他们从主流华语电影中脱颖而出。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "石坂表示，对于“亚洲之窗”的新锐导演来说，东京观众的反馈将直接滋养他们的下一个项目，而与来访的国际节目策划人的会面也常常为他们带来其他电影节的邀请和合拍机会。日本以“微型剧场”（mini-theaters）广为人知的独立艺术影院网络，得到了富有经验的国际电影发行商的支持。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这里的电影节首映直接转化为本土院线发行协议的情况并不罕见，”石坂说，“归根结底，我们的使命是充当积极的跳板，促进这些产业联系。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "石坂的大部分职业生涯都用于研究纪录片以及亚洲与中东之间的文化交流。尽管今年“亚洲之窗”没有非虚构类作品，但他发现过去五年中来自全亚洲的战争纪录片发生了戏剧性的变化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“安装在头盔上的微型数码相机以直观的即视感捕捉惊心动魄的前线经历，产生的画面如此强烈，以至于超越了现实主义，达到了只能称之为‘超现实’的境界，”他说，“这是一个以冲突为标志的时代的视觉语言。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "相比之下，他表示，探讨相同主题的剧情长片似乎正在向隐喻和寓言方向发展。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Family relationships run through the Asian films that Tokyo International Film Festival programmer Ishizaka Kenji has picked for this year’s edition.

“While it is hard to pinpoint an exact catalyst for this surge in family-driven drama, what is undeniable is that amidst today’s geopolitical volatility, these filmmakers share an instinctive urge to reexamine the smallest foundational unit around them: the family and sibling bonds,” Ishizaka tells Variety .

Related Stories

'High Potential' Lands Post-Super Bowl LXI Slot on ABC Next February

Disney Broadens Super Bowl LXI Plans With Pat McAfee, Next-Gen Stats

Ishizaka has programmed Asian cinema at the festival since 2007, when most submissions were still shot on film. Digital took over within a few years. His selection process moved from 35mm prints and VHS tapes to DVDs, and later to streaming links and downloadable screeners.

Popular on Variety

‘The physical medium gave way to data; cinema lost its tangible ‘weight,” he says.

The shift also changed what films looked like. Freed from the need to reload film, Asian directors leaned into long running times built on unbroken takes, and so-called slow cinema spread across the region. Two of its leading auteurs took top prizes at major European festivals in the 2010s: Thailand’s Apichatpong Weerasethakul won the Palme d’Or at Cannes for “Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives,” and the Philippines’ Lav Diaz won Venice’s Golden Lion for “The Woman Who Left.”

Ishizaka also oversees Asian Future, the festival’s competition for young Asian filmmakers. Its 10 titles this year include Katski Flores’ “Edjop” from the Philippines, Kim Hyun-min’s “On the Heights” from South Korea and Chezhiyan’s “The Paper Flower” from India. Azamat Shargyn’s “Shyrmauyq” from Kazakhstan, Ariani Darmawan’s “Jani Be Good” from Indonesia and Kujiraoka Hironori’s “Saravah” from Japan are also in the running.

The line between studio fare and independent film has blurred considerably, he says.

“In the Philippines, for instance – a national cinema often described as enjoying its ‘Third Golden Age’ since 2005 – we are seeing mainstream stars actively board indie projects after falling in love with bold, original scripts,” Ishizaka says. “This has even spawned the portmanteau ‘maindie’ cinema.”

He points to directors Brillante Mendoza and Jun Robles Lana, who switch easily between commercial and small-scale indie work, as key links between the two worlds. Other industries in the region are seeing similar crossover.

If the 2010s belonged to Southeast Asian cinema, the story of the 2020s is still being written. For now, Ishizaka singles out Taiwan and South Korea for the strength of their public funding and institutional backing.

“Thematically, an exciting wave of emerging filmmakers from China’s autonomous regions – Tibet, Inner Mongolia, and Xinjiang – is stepping into the spotlight,” he says. “Mentored and inspired by trailblazing predecessors like the late Pema Tseden, these directors bring distinct regional perspectives and aesthetic sensibilities that set them apart from mainstream Chinese cinema.”

For emerging directors in Asian Future, Ishizaka says, the reactions of Tokyo audiences feed straight into their next projects, while meetings with visiting international programmers regularly lead to invitations from other festivals and co-production opportunities. Japan’s network of independent arthouse venues, known locally as mini-theaters, is supported by experienced distributors of international cinema.

“It is not uncommon for a festival premiere here to translate directly into a domestic theatrical distribution deal,” Ishizaka says. “Ultimately, our mission is to serve as an active springboard that fosters these industry connections.”

Ishizaka has spent much of his career studying documentary film and cultural exchange between Asia and the Middle East. Although Asian Future has no nonfiction titles this year, he sees a dramatic change in war documentaries from across Asia in the last five years.

“Miniature digital cameras mounted on helmets capture the harrowing frontline experience with visceral immediacy, yielding footage so intense it transcends realism into what can only be called the ‘hyper-real,’” he says. “It is the visual language of an era marked by conflict.”

Fiction features tackling the same subjects, by contrast, appear to be moving toward metaphor and allegory, he says.

article_text:
The Greaves family ‘s “ Once Upon a Time in Harlem ” is making waves in this year’s Best Documentary Feature Oscar race — and it’s about to screen for free throughout New York City this weekend.

A day after Neon announced a partnership with The Guardian to expand the theatrical release of another documentary Oscar contender, “ NAZA ,” the company is now partnering with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to bring “ Once Upon a Time in Harlem ” to more audiences.

Four free screenings of the film , co-directed by the late William Greaves with his son David, will roll out on Saturday, October 24, and Sunday, October 25, in New York City. The screenings will take place at the AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, Film Forum, and Film at Lincoln Center, “celebrating the legacy of the Harlem Renaissance and the enduring global power of art, culture, and creativity,” per the announcement.

“’Once Upon a Time in Harlem’ brings the personalities, ideas, and debates behind the Harlem Renaissance to life for a new generation of New Yorkers,” Mamdani said in a statement. “We are proud to partner with the filmmaking team to offer free screenings to New Yorkers this weekend, ensuring that as many New Yorkers as possible get the chance to experience this film. Our city owes a debt of gratitude to the artists of the Harlem Renaissance whose enduring legacy is still felt in every jazz club, in every gallery, and in the movement for social justice that still continues to this day.”

The film premiered at Sundance before moving on to play Cannes, Telluride, Toronto, and New York, among other festivals. Nominated for five Critics Choice Documentary Awards, the film compiles footage William Greaves shot in 1972 of a gathering of Harlem Renaissance luminaries at Duke Ellington’s townhouse. William’s granddaughter, Liani Greaves, produced the film, with her father David co-directing. Before the younger Greaves took on the project, William’s wife, Louise Archambault, worked tirelessly to bring it to life after William died in 2014. Louise died in 2023.

“William Greaves believed deeply in the power of art to preserve history as well as inspire audiences and future generations. We know it would have meant so much to him to see Mayor Mamdani and the Office of the Mayor champion this film and help bring it to New Yorkers and especially back to Harlem where he was born and raised,” said David and Liani Greaves.

The screening schedule is as follows. RSVP for free tickets here .

Saturday, October 24

1:00 PM at AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, 2309 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027

4:45 PM at Film Forum, 209 W Houston St, New York, NY 10014

Sunday, October 25

1:00 PM at AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, 2309 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027

3:45 PM at Howard Gilman Theater, Film at Lincoln Center, 144 W 65th St, New York, NY 10023

The work is an artificial palm tree whose crown rotates continuously, recalling at once the showy foliage at theme parks and the threadbare lexicon of “the tropical,” “the exotic.” Installed in the broad, hushed garden of the Hoam Museum of Art, Youn’s palm blends into the greenery rather easily. It is legibly about cliché, tourist fantasy, extractive capital, and diasporic belonging, and yet, equally a spot for the selfie—the sort that might attract couples and families who drive out past Seoul’s outskirts on a weekend. The catalog describes the piece as “an antenna receiving signals of exoticism.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The work is a useful entry into this year’s edition of Art Spectrum, which is titled, in a single compacted string, “ARoomWhereEveryRadioIsTunedToDifferentStations.” The biennial exhibition moves away from its previous iteration, which took as its subject the holistic idea of the “screen,” instead adopting a polyphonic approach to position itself as “an undivided space filled with many different sounds and frequencies,” if we agree to take the works of each of the 23 participating artists and collectives—most housed within the museum, several dispersed across its grounds—as antennas of sorts. This feeling of undividedness, at least for me, is heightened by the elision of gaps in the title, which withholds a declarative cadence and nudges the phrase toward estrangement."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "These days, most large-scale surveys or biennales feel obliged to generate an ambitious intellectual output, whether to decenter Western, human-centric, extractivist paradigms, or to usher forward alternative epistemologies, cosmologies, Indigenous knowledge, and spirituality. One of Art Spectrum 2026’s stated inquiries, on the other hand, is simply how practices formed in divergent cultural and social conditions might be brought into conversation under the geographic category of “Asia.” Yet the show is conscious that “Asia” or “contemporary art in Asia” is not a stable or rigid category; that’s why it defines the region as a frequency spectrum, and conceives the exhibition as a receptive space."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/11/24-SIDE-CORE-01.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "SIDE CORE ,"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "time gate , 2021, signboard of parking lot, 730 × 330 × 270 cm, at Art Spectrum, Hoam Museum of Art, Yongin, 2026. Courtesy the Hoam Museum of Art."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The exhibition begins in the parking lot. Arriving visitors are met first by SIDE CORE’s time gate (2021), an assembly of the branded “Times” parking signs common on Japanese streets. It grew out of the collective’s attention to Tokyo’s transient urban fabric and the disruptions and delays around the 2020 Olympics. The work was first staged on a vacant lot near the Olympic stadium. A short walk away, on a stretch of lawn, is Aerin Hong’s commission Music Siren (duet) (2026). Like Youn, Hong is drawn to how nonhuman life can be translated into unfamiliar artistic form. Two life-like toy butterflies beat their wings inside a vitrine, driven by a pair of motors; infrared sensors track the motion, the reflected light registers as vibration, and a sequence of devices converts it, eventually, into piano tone. Through this sleight of hand, the source of movement is prised apart from the source of sound, so that what we see and what we hear never quite align."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Once inside the exhibition space, we encounter SIDE CORE again, in rode work ver. under city (2023), a multichannel video that follows a group of skaters through Tokyo’s subterranean infrastructure, from stormwater reservoirs and decommissioned tunnels to maintenance corridors.
